rationale.conceptual: The method is the paper's own Vicinal Cellular Automaton, which combines diffusion governed by a potential landscape (potential well, Ehrlich-Schwoebel barrier) with Cellular Automaton incorporation rules (critical nucleus sizes). Translating this into a correct simulation requires careful handling of multiple interacting components and non-trivial physics (probabilities, boundary conditions, scaling analysis). It's an established but non-trivial method needing genuine understanding.
rationale.execution: The task involves implementing the full VicCA model, running ~96 simulations (each up to 10^6 time steps on a 300x400 lattice), recording height maps over time, computing directional height-height correlation functions, extracting time series of wavelengths and amplitudes, fitting scaling laws, and classifying morphologies. This forms a multi-stage pipeline with moderate engineering complexity, all within standard Python libraries.

difficulty.reasoning: The VicCA model is a custom, multi-parameter cellular automaton with energy barriers and specific incorporation rules; implementing it correctly requires a solid understanding of the paper's physics. The task requires running a parameter sweep, computing correlation functions, extracting scaling exponents, and classifying morphologies — a multi-stage but straightforward pipeline.

compute_estimate.reasoning: CPU-only lattice simulations with tiny per-run memory (~MB); no external dataset, synthetic data only. Peak memory modest even with multiple parallel runs. The reference solve writes hardcoded paper values, confirming compute cost is manageable on a workstation.
